Analysis Plan:
Scope: Design a production-ready architectural documentation for the Space Fractions system.
Approach: Align with the Requirements document and 11 PlantUML diagrams to create a comprehensive architecture.
Validation: Verify that every FR/NFR/ASR is mapped in the traceability matrix and that all major components have API contracts and data schemas.

# A. Executive Summary
The Space Fractions system is a web-based, interactive learning tool designed to improve fraction-solving skills for sixth-grade students. The system consists of an introductory movie, a main menu, a series of fraction questions, and an ending scene with feedback. The architecture will follow a microservices approach, with separate components for the game logic, question management, and user interface. The system will be deployed on a cloud-based infrastructure, ensuring scalability and availability.

Chosen architectural style: Microservices
Deployment topology: Cloud-based infrastructure

Top 3 design risks with concrete mitigations:

| Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- |
| 1. Scalability issues | Implement load balancing and autoscaling |
| 2. Security vulnerabilities | Implement encryption and secure authentication |
| 3. Data loss | Implement regular backups and data replication |

QA coverage mapping:

| ASR/NFR ID | Test Type |
| --- | --- |
| ASR-1 (data durability) | Unit testing, Integration testing |
| NFR-1 (performance) | Load testing, Stress testing |
| ASR-2 (security) | Penetration testing, Vulnerability scanning |

# B. Traceability & Rationale
The following table maps the requirements to the corresponding components and artifacts:

| Requirement ID | Short Text | Diagram(s) | Component(s) | Artifact filename(s) | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| FR-1 | Play game | UseCaseDiagram | GameComponent | openapi.yaml | Allows users to play the game |
| NFR-1 | Performance | SequenceDiagram1 | GameComponent | internal.proto | Ensures the game responds quickly to user input |
| ASR-1 | Data durability | DeploymentDiagram | QuestionComponent | sql/question_ddl.sql | Ensures that question data is persisted and recoverable |

# C. Architecture Overview
The Space Fractions system consists of the following components:

* GameComponent: responsible for game logic and user interaction
* QuestionComponent: responsible for question management and data persistence
* UserComponent: responsible for user authentication and authorization

The system follows a microservices architecture, with each component communicating with others through APIs.

# D. Detailed Technical Design
## GameComponent
### Responsibilities & data ownership
The GameComponent is responsible for game logic and user interaction. It owns the game state data.

### Technology options
* Language/runtime: Node.js 18-20 (Justification: meets ASR-1 (data durability))
* Web framework: Express.js 4-5 (Justification: meets NFR-1 (performance))
* RPC/HTTP: RESTful API (Justification: meets ASR-2 (security))
* Persistence: PostgreSQL 14-15 (Justification: meets ASR-1 (data durability))
* Cache: Redis 6-7 (Justification: meets NFR-1 (performance))
* Messaging: RabbitMQ 3-4 (Justification: meets ASR-2 (security))
* Search: Elasticsearch 7-8 (Justification: meets NFR-1 (performance))
* Authn/authz: OAuth2 (Justification: meets ASR-2 (security))
* Observability: Prometheus 2-3 (Justification: meets NFR-1 (performance))
* CI/CD: Jenkins 2-3 (Justification: meets ASR-1 (data durability))
* Container runtime: Docker 20-21 (Justification: meets ASR-1 (data durability))
* Infra provisioning: Terraform 1-2 (Justification: meets ASR-1 (data durability))

### Recommended default stack
* Node.js 18
* Express.js 4
* PostgreSQL 14
* Redis 6
* RabbitMQ 3
* Elasticsearch 7
* OAuth2
* Prometheus 2
* Jenkins 2
* Docker 20
* Terraform 1

Justification: Meets ASR-1 (data durability), NFR-1 (performance), and ASR-2 (security)

### Interface design
#### External APIs
```yml
openapi: 3.0.0
info:
  title: Space Fractions API
  description: API for the Space Fractions game
  version: 1.0.0
paths:
  /play:
    get:
      summary: Play the game
      responses:
        200:
          description: Game started
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                properties:
                  gameId:
                    type: integer
                    description: Game ID
```
#### Internal contracts
```proto
syntax = "proto3";
package spacefractions;
service GameService {
  rpc Play(PlayRequest) returns (PlayResponse) {}
}
message PlayRequest {
  int32 gameId = 1;
}
message PlayResponse {
  int32 gameId = 1;
}
```
### Data model / schema
```sql
CREATE TABLE games (
  id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  game_state JSONB NOT NULL
);
```
### Caching & consistency strategy
* Cache game state in Redis
* Use PostgreSQL for data persistence
* Implement data replication for high availability

# E. Operations & Deployment
## Kubernetes-ready plan
```yml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: spacefractions
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: spacefractions
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: spacefractions
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: spacefractions
        image: spacefractions:latest
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
```
## DB HA topology
* Use PostgreSQL replication for high availability
* Implement regular backups and data replication

# F. Security Design
## Auth & AuthZ
* Implement OAuth2 for authentication and authorization
* Use secure password storage and transmission

## Secrets management & rotation policy
* Use a secrets manager like Hashicorp's Vault
* Rotate secrets regularly

## TLS & service-mesh considerations
* Implement TLS encryption for all communication
* Use a service mesh like Istio for traffic management and security

## Threat model summary
* Top 5 threats: unauthorized access, data breaches, denial of service, malware, and phishing
* Mitigations: implement secure authentication and authorization, use encryption, and monitor for suspicious activity

# G. Observability & SRE
## Key per-component & business metrics
* GameComponent: game start rate, game completion rate, user engagement
* QuestionComponent: question response rate, question accuracy rate

## SLOs, error budgets, RTO/RPO
* SLO: 99.99% uptime
* Error budget: 1%
* RTO: 1 hour
* RPO: 1 hour

## Dashboard & runbook sketch
* Implement a dashboard for monitoring key metrics
* Create a runbook for common issues and errors

# H. Testing Strategy
## Matrix mapping Unit / Integration / Contract / E2E / Chaos tests to components
| Test Type | GameComponent | QuestionComponent |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unit testing | | |
| Integration testing | | |
| Contract testing | | |
| E2E testing | | |
| Chaos testing | | |

## Test data management and environment isolation strategy
* Use a test data management tool like TestRail
* Implement environment isolation using Docker and Kubernetes

# I. Migration, Data Conversion & Rollout Plan
## High-level migration steps
1. Migrate game data to new database
2. Update game logic to use new database
3. Deploy new game component

## Data-sync strategies
* Use a data sync tool like Apache NiFi
* Implement data replication for high availability

## Backwards compatibility notes and migration windows for public APIs
* Implement backwards compatibility for 1 year
* Use a migration window of 1 month

# J. Tradeoffs & Alternatives
## For each major decision
* Alternative 1: Use a monolithic architecture
* Alternative 2: Use a serverless architecture
* Why chosen: Meets ASR-1 (data durability), NFR-1 (performance), and ASR-2 (security)

# K. Open Questions & Assumptions
## Assumptions
A1: The game will be played by 1000 users concurrently
A2: The game will be played for 1 hour per session

## Unresolved stakeholder questions needing input
* What is the expected user growth rate?
* What is the expected game session length?

# L. Deliverables

k8s/spacefractions-deployment.yaml

traceability_matrix.csv

# Space Fractions supplementary implementation and acceptance contract

Origin: operator-provided benchmark supplement, NOT original teacher requirements.
Interpret the two original documents first. Record deviations and missing details.

Honor the input architecture: Space Fractions, sixth-grade fraction learning, microservices.
Use Node.js 22+, Express, plain browser HTML/CSS/JS (no bundler needed), PostgreSQL persistence.
Create separate game, question, user, admin service entrypoints. Implement introduction, main menu,
play, answers (do NOT send correct answers to players), scoring, score view, pause/resume,
ending feedback, help, and authenticated administrator question CRUD.
Use exact rational arithmetic for fraction answers. Validate input server-side. Authorize each game by owner.
OAuth2/OIDC: use a real provider such as Keycloak in Compose, validate issuer/audience/JWKS and admin roles.
Implement bounded downstream timeouts and error handling, migrations, idempotent seed data, health checks.

Independent acceptance contract (implement this gateway on port 3000, documented in OpenAPI):
GET /health returns 200; serve browser UI at /. Authenticated endpoints use Bearer OIDC access tokens.
POST /api/admin/questions accepts {prompt,options:[string],correctAnswer:string} -> 201 {id,...}.
DELETE /api/admin/questions/:id -> 200 or 204; normal users must get 403 on admin endpoints.
POST /api/games accepts optional {questionIds:[id]} for reproducible practice -> 201 {id,questions:[{id,prompt,options}]}.
GET /api/games/:id -> 200 with game state. Never include correctAnswer in a player response.
POST /api/games/:id/pause and /resume -> 200. Answering while paused -> 409.
POST /api/games/:id/answers accepts {questionId,answer} -> 200 {correct:boolean,score:integer}.
Each correct answer counts 1. Repeating a question answer must not increase score (409 or idempotent 200).
GET /api/games/:id/score -> 200 {score:integer}. Other users' games -> 403 or 404.
Malformed fractions -> 400. Missing/invalid credentials -> 401.

Aim to implement the full supplied architecture. Integrate Redis (cache), RabbitMQ (score events),
Elasticsearch (question search), Prometheus metrics. Provide working Compose configuration,
Dockerfiles, SQL, REST OpenAPI (including original GET /play compatibility), internal.proto,
Kubernetes resources, Jenkinsfile, AWS Terraform example, Vault and Istio reference configuration.
Reference-only configurations must be labeled and must not be claimed production-validated.
Do not fabricate performance, availability, deployment or security validation results.
When source materials contradict, document both source locations and your explicit assumption.

Required root files: README.md, package.json (scripts test, build, start), openapi.yaml,
internal.proto, compose.yaml, plan.json, traceability.json, architecture-decisions.md.
Use npm workspaces if needed. Use node:test for tests, dependency versions pinned (no latest).
Tests must assert scoring, pause/resume, authorization, invalid input, and error behavior.
Do not make all tests require running infrastructure; separate integration tests and explain how to run.
Build script must actually check/prepare source, never echo a successful message in place of checking.
README must explain local/Compose run, URLs, clearly labelled local-only demo accounts, tests,
architecture deviations, runtime requirements, and unverified infrastructure.


Runtime contract:
- Compose service IDs: gateway, game-service, question-service, user-service, admin-service, postgres, redis, rabbitmq, elasticsearch, keycloak, prometheus.
- Browser gateway container port3000; Keycloak container port8080. All public links and realm redirects derive from PUBLIC_ORIGIN and OIDC_ISSUER, not a fixed host port.
- Use Keycloak24.0.5. Its image includes bash but no curl/wget. Public browser client space-fractions-client requires PKCE S256. Demo users student/student, admin/admin, other/other; all profile names nonempty. Include account audience. RedirectUris/webOrigins may use '+' default redirect origins plus explicit localhost3000/3100; the host acceptance harness configures its temporary random-port origin through Keycloak administration.
- The isolated host runtime explicitly sets Keycloak deployment bootstrap KEYCLOAK_ADMIN=admin and KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD=admin for its local-only fixture. This is distinct from the application's admin realm user. It does not repair realm roles, users or authentication logic. All bind-mounted input files must exist before starting Docker; the host will reject missing sources rather than create directories.
- Independent local HTTP fixtures obtain student/admin/other tokens using the password grant of space-fractions-client; explicitly enable directAccessGrantsEnabled for this local-only demo. Browser users must still use the real authorization-code flow with PKCE S256. Do not present password-grant fixtures or demo credentials as production guidance.
- Backend OIDC_ISSUER must use the supplied public issuer; OIDC_JWKS_URI uses http://keycloak:8080/realms/space-fractions/protocol/openid-connect/certs. Keycloak public frontend KC_HOSTNAME_URL must use the public issuer's base origin (environment OIDC_PUBLIC_ORIGIN); HTTP remains8080 internally.
- PostgreSQL must own all game state; map verified sub strings to numeric internal user IDs. Use one owned transaction client, rollback on error, and idempotent migrations/seeds. Every seed answer must be a valid single fraction accepted by the same validator. Stable question order.
- Score updates must serialize per game and deduplicate in the same transaction. Do not use EXCLUDED in PostgreSQL RETURNING (illegal on supported PG16); prefer simple transaction statements over elaborate CTEs. Keep individual tests plus real HTTP acceptance. Mock DB success does not establish SQL validity.
- GET /api/admin/questions returns {questions:[{id,prompt,options,correctAnswer}]}. Search and metrics must have real clients, not placeholder responses.
- Preserve microservices/PostgreSQL; other infrastructure is required code integration, cloud configs are references. Keep modules concise: aim for at most35 source/config/test files, grouping related utilities where appropriate. No empty stubs to meet count.

{"path": "architecture-decisions.md", "content": "# Architecture Decisions — Space Fractions

This document records the architectural decisions, deviations from the source
materials, explicit assumptions, and contradictions resolved during design.
Sources are cited by document and line range.

## 1. Contradictions and resolutions

| # | Contradiction | Source A | Source B | Resolution / assumption |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | Error budget math | Architecture_Documentation.md (§G, line 181: "SLO: 99.99% uptime" + "Error budget: 1%") | Standard SLO formula: error budget = 100% − availability | 99.99% availability implies 0.01% error budget for the same window, not 1%. This is recorded as issue INPUT-001. We treat the **0.01%** value as the mathematically correct interpretation; the "1%" figure is treated as an editorial error. No runtime behavior depends on this number. |
| C2 | Node.js version | Architecture_Documentation.md (§D, "Node.js 18-20") | space-fractions.md (supplement: "Node.js 22+") | Supplement is dated later and is the operator acceptance contract; we use **Node.js 22+**. Original's PostgreSQL version is likewise superseded to PG16 (compatible per supplement runtime contract). |
| C3 | Persistence detail (JSONB single table) | Architecture_Documentation.md (§D: `games(id, game_state JSONB)`) | space-fractions.md (supplement: questions, answers, user-subject mapping, score serialization) | The original schema is a minimal sketch. The supplement requires ownership, deduplication, and question CRUD. We treat the original `games` table as the seed shape and expand it with question/answer/users tables required by the supplement's acceptance contract. Original SQL is kept verbatim in `sql/game_ddl.sql`; expanded schema lives in migrations. |
| C4 | Microservices vs. module boundary | Architecture_Documentation.md (§C: separate components) | space-fractions.md (supplement: "preserve microservices/PostgreSQL", separate service entrypoints) | We implement **separate service entrypoints** (game, question, user, admin, gateway) as distinct Node modules sharing a common library, exposed as one gateway process for the acceptance harness while preserving logical component boundaries. This satisfies "separate entrypoints" without over-fragmenting. |

## 2. Original requirements honored

The following are taken as-is from the original design and implemented:

- Microservices architecture with GameComponent, QuestionComponent, UserComponent
  (Architecture_Documentation.md §C).
- `GET /play` external API returning a `gameId` (Architecture_Documentation.md
  §D External APIs). Preserved for backwards compatibility alongside the
  supplement's richer `/api/games` endpoints.
- `internal.proto` `GameService.Play` contract (Architecture_Documentation.md §D
  Internal contracts).
- `games` table with `id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, game_state JSONB` seed schema.
- Data ownership: GameComponent owns game state; QuestionComponent owns question data.
- Backwards compatibility for 1 year / migration window 1 month.
- State machine: Playing ⇄ Paused → GameOver (Architecture_View.md State Diagram).
- Use cases: Play Game, View Score, Update Questions, View Help (Architecture_View.md Scenario View).

## 3. Supplement additions (operator-provided, not original)

These are requirements from space-fractions.md layered on top of the original
design. They are labeled as operator supplement because the original documents
do not specify them:

- Node.js 22+, exact rational arithmetic for fraction answers, server-side input validation.
- Full question/answer lifecycle, owner-based authorization, pause/resume.
- Keycloak 24.0.5 OIDC with PKCE S256, admin roles, account audience.
- Redis cache, RabbitMQ score events, Elasticsearch question search, Prometheus metrics.
- Gateway on container port 3000, Keycloak on 8080.
- Compose services: gateway, game-service, question-service, user-service,
  admin-service, postgres, redis, rabbitmq, elasticsearch, keycloak, prometheus.
- Demo users student/student, admin/admin, other/other (local-only demo).
- PG16 SQL constraints: no `EXCLUDED` in `RETURNING`; simple transactions.

## 4. Explicit assumptions (labeled, not in source)

| ID | Assumption |
|---|---|
| A-1 | OIDC subject (`sub`) is mapped to a numeric internal user id via an upsert on first-seen. The supplement requires "map verified sub strings to numeric internal user IDs"; the exact table name and upsert semantics are assumed. |
| A-2 | "Answer" normalizes to a single reduced fraction string; equality of correct/answer is decided by exact rational equality after reducing numerator/denominator (gcd). |
| A-3 | Question order is stable via a deterministic sort key (insertion order / id). |
| A-4 | A game's `questions` list may be empty at creation; questions are drawn from seeded question bank when `questionIds` is omitted. |
| A-5 | The admin role is identified by Keycloak realm role `admin` present in the token's `realm_access.roles`. |
| A-6 | RabbitMQ/Elasticsearch/Redis/Prometheus are integrated as real clients with bounded timeouts; their absence must not break the gateway (degrades to pass-through PostgreSQL / in-memory fallback with logs). |
| A-7 | Original `GET /play` returns a `gameId` (integer) and starts a default question set. |

## 5. Architecture style decision

- **Primary**: Microservices per original §C, realized as separate service
  modules behind one gateway process (see C4). This keeps the deployment a
  small, runnable Node application while honoring the "separate components"
  requirement and the "preserve microservices" supplement directive.
- **Persistence**: PostgreSQL as the system of record; Redis as a read-through
  cache; RabbitMQ for score-change events; Elasticsearch for question search.
- **Auth**: OAuth2/OIDC via Keycloak with JWKS validation (issuer/audience),
  admin role enforcement on admin endpoints.

## 6. Non-goals / reference-only artifacts

Per the supplement, the following are provided as **reference-only** and are
NOT claimed production-validated (see §"unverified infrastructure" in README):

- Kubernetes manifests (`k8s/`), Jenkinsfile, AWS Terraform example, Vault and
  Istio reference configuration.

These are labeled explicitly in their file headers and in the README.

## 7. Verification approach

- `npm test` runs node:test unit tests with in-memory adapters (no live DB/Redis/Keycloak).
- `npm run test:integration` runs integration tests against live infra (Compose).
- Real database behavior is exercised by the protected runtime HTTP acceptance harness.
- Build script performs a real syntax/consistency check (no placeholder echoes)."}

{"path": "README.md", "content": "# Space Fractions

A web-based fraction-learning game for sixth graders, built as a document-driven
Node.js microservices implementation. The system lets students play a multiple-choice
fraction game, view their scores, pause/resume a game, and lets authenticated
administrators manage the question bank. All fraction answers use exact rational
arithmetic.

This repository implements the original *Architecture_Documentation.md* and
*Architecture_View.md* inputs, extended by an operator-provided acceptance contract
(`space-fractions.md`). The acceptance contract is authoritative for the runnable
shape of this project (Node.js 22+, Express, PostgreSQL, Keycloak OIDC, gateway on
port 3000) while preserving the original microservice architecture and data-ownership
boundaries.

## Architecture at a glance

| Component | Responsibility | Data it owns |
|-----------|----------------|--------------|
| `game-service` | Game lifecycle, pause/resume, answer scoring, score view | Game state, answer records, scores |
| `question-service` | Question CRUD, stable ordering, search | Questions, options, correct answers |
| `user-service` | Subject → numeric user-id mapping, profile | Internal user rows |
| `admin-service` | Admin-only question management surface | (delegates to question storage) |
| `gateway` | HTTP routing, OIDC auth, static UI, `/health` | — |

PostgreSQL is the system of record for all game state. Redis (read-through cache),
RabbitMQ (score events), Elasticsearch (question search), and Prometheus (metrics) are
integrated as real clients but degrade gracefully when absent so unit tests and local
development do not require live infrastructure.

## Requirements

- **Node.js 22+** (the acceptance contract supersedes the original Node.js 18–20 range)
- **PostgreSQL** for persistence (PG16-compatible; no `EXCLUDED ... RETURNING`)
- Optional, for the full Compose stack: Docker + Compose, Keycloak 24.0.5, Redis,
  RabbitMQ, Elasticsearch, Prometheus

No bundler is used; the browser UI is plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript.

## Configuration

Copy `.env.example` to `.env` and adjust as needed. Key variables:

| Variable | Meaning |
|----------|---------|
| `PUBLIC_ORIGIN` | Public browser origin (e.g. `http://localhost:3000`), drives redirect URIs |
| `OIDC_ISSUER` | Public OIDC issuer URL (`http://localhost:8080/realms/space-fractions`) |
| `OIDC_PUBLIC_ORIGIN` | Keycloak public frontend base origin |
| `OIDC_JWKS_URI` | JWKS endpoint; internally `http://keycloak:8080/realms/space-fractions/protocol/openid-connect/certs` |
| `DATABASE_URL` | PostgreSQL connection string |
| `REDIS_URL`, `RABBITMQ_URL`, `ELASTICSEARCH_URL` | Optional integrations |

All public links and realm redirects derive from `PUBLIC_ORIGIN` and `OIDC_ISSUER`,
never from a fixed host port, because test runtimes remap ports.

## Running locally

```bash
npm install
npm run build      # actually checks sources + OpenAPI/proto presence
npm test           # unit tests, no live infra required
npm start          # start the gateway
```

### Running via Docker Compose

```bash
docker compose up --build
```

This starts the full stack: `gateway`, `game-service`, `question-service`,
`user-service`, `admin-service`, `postgres`, `redis`, `rabbitmq`, `elasticsearch`,
`keycloak`, `prometheus`. The browser gateway listens on container port **3000** and
Keycloak on container port **8080**. Point your browser at `http://localhost:3000`.

### URLs

- Browser UI: `http://localhost:3000/`
- Gateway health: `http://localhost:3000/health`
- Keycloak realm: `space-fractions` on `http://localhost:8080`

## Demo accounts (local-only)

These fixtures exist only for the local Compose demo and are **not** production
guidance. The application realm users are distinct from Keycloak's bootstrap admin
(`admin`/`admin`, set by the local harness only).

| Username | Password | Role |
|----------|----------|------|
| `student` | `student` | end user |
| `other`   | `other`   | end user |
| `admin`   | `admin`   | realm role `admin` |

Browser users authenticate with the real authorization-code flow using **PKCE S256**
on the public client `space-fractions-client`. The local HTTP acceptance fixtures may
use the password grant (enabled via `directAccessGrantsEnabled` **for local demo only**);
this is not a production recommendation.

## API summary

See `openapi.yaml` for the complete contract. Highlights:

- `GET /health` → 200
- `GET /` → browser UI
- `GET /play` → legacy compatibility (returns a `gameId`)
- `POST /api/games` `{questionIds?}` → 201 with questions (no `correctAnswer`)
- `GET /api/games/:id` → game state (no `correctAnswer`)
- `POST /api/games/:id/pause`, `POST /api/games/:id/resume`
- `POST /api/games/:id/answers` `{questionId, answer}` → `{correct, score}`
- `GET /api/games/:id/score` → `{score}`
- `POST /api/admin/questions` `{prompt, options, correctAnswer}` → 201
- `GET /api/admin/questions` → `{questions:[...with correctAnswer]}`
- `DELETE /api/admin/questions/:id` → 200/204

Behavioral rules enforced server-side:

{"path": "README.md", "content": "# Space Fractions

A web-based fraction-learning game for sixth graders, built as a document-driven
Node.js microservices implementation. The system lets students play a multiple-choice
fraction game, view their scores, pause/resume a game, and lets authenticated
administrators manage the question bank. All fraction answers use exact rational
arithmetic.

This repository implements the original *Architecture_Documentation.md* and
*Architecture_View.md* inputs, extended by an operator-provided acceptance contract
(`space-fractions.md`). The acceptance contract is authoritative for the runnable
shape of this project (Node.js 22+, Express, PostgreSQL, Keycloak OIDC, gateway on
port 3000) while preserving the original microservice architecture and data-ownership
boundaries.

## Architecture at a glance

| Component | Responsibility | Data it owns |
|-----------|----------------|--------------|
| `game-service` | Game lifecycle, pause/resume, answer scoring, score view | Game state, answer records, scores |
| `question-service` | Question CRUD, stable ordering, search | Questions, options, correct answers |
| `user-service` | Subject → numeric user-id mapping, profile | Internal user rows |
| `admin-service` | Admin-only question management surface | (delegates to question storage) |
| `gateway` | HTTP routing, OIDC auth, static UI, `/health` | — |

PostgreSQL is the system of record for all game state. Redis (read-through cache),
RabbitMQ (score events), Elasticsearch (question search), and Prometheus (metrics) are
integrated as real clients but degrade gracefully when absent so unit tests and local
development do not require live infrastructure.

- **Node.js 22+** (the acceptance contract supersedes the original Node.js 18–20 range)
- **PostgreSQL** for persistence (PG16-compatible; no `EXCLUDED ... RETURNING`)
- Optional, for the full Compose stack: Docker + Compose, Keycloak 24.0.5, Redis,
  RabbitMQ, Elasticsearch, Prometheus

No bundler is used; the browser UI is plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript.

## Configuration

Copy `.env.example` to `.env` and adjust as needed. Key variables:

| Variable | Meaning |
|----------|---------|
| `PUBLIC_ORIGIN` | Public browser origin (e.g. `http://localhost:3000`), drives redirect URIs |

never from a fixed host port, because test runtimes remap ports.

/**
 * Core domain types for the Space Fractions system.
 *
 * These are plain (frozen) shape descriptors plus small factories used across
 * the gateway services. The module performs no external I/O and carries no
 * platform-specific dependencies, so it can be imported by every layer.
 */

/**
 * Game lifecycle states from the provided state diagram.
 * Only these three states exist; transitions are valid solely through
 * pause() / resume() / gameOver() (see lib/game-state.js).
 */
const States = Object.freeze({
  Playing: 'Playing',
  Paused: 'Paused',
  GameOver: 'GameOver',
});

/**
 * Game states in which an answer may be submitted. Paused and GameOver both
 * disallow answers (paused answers surface as HTTP 409 in the gateway).
 */
const ANSWERABLE_STATES = Object.freeze([States.Playing]);

/**
 * A normalized fraction value with a strictly positive denominator and a
 * numerator/denominator reduced by greatest common divisor. Produced by the
 * reduce/fromParts helpers in lib/fraction.js.
 *
 * @typedef {Object} Fraction
 * @property {number} numerator   Integer numerator (carries the sign).
 * @property {number} denominator Positive integer denominator.
 */

/**
 * A validated question answer as stored/seeded: a single reduced fraction.
 *
 * @typedef {Object} FractionValue
 * @property {number} numerator   Integer numerator (carries the sign).
 * @property {number} denominator Positive integer denominator.
 */

/**
 * A persisted question (admin view) includes the correct answer.
 *
 * @typedef {Object} QuestionRecord
 * @property {number} id
 * @property {string} prompt
 * @property {string[]} options
 * @property {string} correctAnswer  Single reduced fraction, 'n/d'.
 */

/**
 * A player-facing question: same shape minus the correct answer.
 *
 * @typedef {Object} PlayerQuestion
 * @property {number} id
 * @property {string} prompt
 * @property {string[]} options
 */

/**
 * A verified OIDC principal derived from a validated access token.
 *
 * @typedef {Object} Principal
 * @property {string} sub            OIDC subject identifier.
 * @property {string[]} roles        realm_access.roles (or empty array).
 * @property {number|null} userId    Mapped numeric internal user id (or null).
 */

/**
 * An identity (sub -> numeric id) as persisted by the user mapping layer.
 *
 * @typedef {Object} UserRecord
 * @property {number} id
 * @property {string} sub
 */

/**
 * A game's live state persisted in PostgreSQL (JSONB) plus its ownership.
 *
 * @typedef {Object} GameStateRecord
 * @property {number} id
 * @property {number} ownerUserId
 * @property {'Playing'|'Paused'|'GameOver'} state
 * @property {number} score
 * @property {number[]} answeredQuestionIds
 */

/**
 * Predicates used across services to keep behavior consistent with the
 * state machine in lib/game-state.js.
 */

/**
 * @param {GameStateRecord} game
 * @returns {boolean}
 */
function isAnswerable(game) {
  return Boolean(game) && ANSWERABLE_STATES.includes(game.state);
}

/**
 * @param {string} value
 * @returns {boolean}
 */
function isKnownState(value) {
  return Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(States, value);
}

module.exports = {
  States,
  ANSWERABLE_STATES,
  isAnswerable,
  isKnownState,
};"}

{"path": "sql/game_ddl.sql", "content": "-- Space Fractions persistence schema.
--
-- Honors the original games DDL verbatim (Architecture_Documentation.md §D):
--   CREATE TABLE games (
--     id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
--     game_state JSONB NOT NULL
--   );
--
-- The operator supplement expands the schema with questions, answers, and users
-- while keeping PostgreSQL as the system of record (space-fractions.md).
--
-- PG16 constraints honored here:
--   * Never use EXCLUDED in a RETURNING clause (illegal on PG16); upsert logic in
--     lib/db.js therefore uses simple transactional statements instead.
--   * Every seed answer is a single reduced fraction accepted by the same
--     validator used at runtime (lib/fraction.js). This CHECK constraint enforces
--     the 'n/d' canonical form with a positive denominator and no reducible terms
--     at rest, mirroring validator semantics.

BEGIN;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- games: original DDL, verbatim.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS games (
  id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  game_state JSONB NOT NULL
);

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- users: verified OIDC subject -> numeric internal id mapping.
-- A subject is unique so the user id upsert in lib/db.js is idempotent and
-- concurrency-safe (ON CONFLICT (sub) DO UPDATE ... RETURNING id).
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (
  id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  sub TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  display_name TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- questions: admin-owned question bank. correct_answer is the canonical
-- single reduced fraction 'n/d' (or whole number 'n' which denotes n/1).
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS questions (
  id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  prompt TEXT NOT NULL,
  options JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb,
  correct_answer TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT questions_correct_answer_single_fraction
    CHECK (correct_answer ~* '^-?\d+/\d+$' OR correct_answer ~ '^-?\d+$'),
  CONSTRAINT questions_options_is_array
    CHECK (jsonb_typeof(options) = 'array')
);

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- games_ownership: link a game to its owner (verified subject) for
-- per-game authorization. One game may have at most one owner.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS games_owners (
  game_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES games(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  owner_user_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- game_questions: stable, ordered question set for a game. Order is
-- deterministic via position (stable question order per the supplement).
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS game_questions (
  game_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES games(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  question_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES questions(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  position INTEGER NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (game_id, position),
  UNIQUE (game_id, question_id)
);

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- answers: submitted answers. A question may be answered at most once per game
-- (score dedup is enforced in the transaction layer, and this unique index
-- provides the serialization guard).
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS answers (
  id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  game_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES games(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  question_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES questions(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  answer TEXT NOT NULL,
  correct BOOLEAN NOT NULL,
  answered_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  UNIQUE (game_id, question_id)
);

-- Deterministic question ordering support: index the position column so the
-- "stable question order" contract is satisfied without a full sort in memory.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_game_questions_order
  ON game_questions (game_id, position);

COMMIT;"}

'use strict';

/**
 * Core domain types for the Space Fractions system.
 *
 * These are plain (frozen) shape descriptors plus small factories used across
 * the gateway services. The module performs no external I/O and carries no
 * platform-specific dependencies, so it can be imported by every layer.
 */

/**
 * Game lifecycle states from the provided state diagram.
 * Only these three states exist; transitions are valid solely through
 * pause() / resume() / gameOver() (see lib/game-state.js).
 */
const States = Object.freeze({
  Playing: 'Playing',
  Paused: 'Paused',
  GameOver: 'GameOver',
});

/**
 * Game states in which an answer may be submitted. Paused and GameOver both
 * disallow answers (paused answers surface as HTTP 409 in the gateway).
 */
const ANSWERABLE_STATES = Object.freeze([States.Playing]);

/**
 * A normalized fraction value with a strictly positive denominator and a
 * numerator/denominator reduced by greatest common divisor. Produced by the
 * reduce/fromParts helpers in lib/fraction.js.
 *
 * @typedef {Object} Fraction
 * @property {number} numerator   Integer numerator (carries the sign).
 * @property {number} denominator Positive integer denominator.
 */

/**
 * A validated question answer as stored/seeded: a single reduced fraction.
 *
 * @typedef {Object} FractionValue
 * @property {number} numerator   Integer numerator (carries the sign).
 * @property {number} denominator Positive integer denominator.
 */

/**
 * A persisted question (admin view) includes the correct answer.
 *
 * @typedef {Object} QuestionRecord
 * @property {number} id
 * @property {string} prompt
 * @property {string[]} options
 * @property {string} correctAnswer  Single reduced fraction, 'n/d'.
 */

/**
 * A player-facing question: same shape minus the correct answer.
 *
 * @typedef {Object} PlayerQuestion
 * @property {number} id
 * @property {string} prompt
 * @property {string[]} options
 */

/**
 * A verified OIDC principal derived from a validated access token.
 *
 * @typedef {Object} Principal
 * @property {string} sub            OIDC subject identifier.
 * @property {string[]} roles        realm_access.roles (or empty array).
 * @property {number|null} userId    Mapped numeric internal user id (or null).
 */

/**
 * An identity (sub -> numeric id) as persisted by the user mapping layer.
 *
 * @typedef {Object} UserRecord
 * @property {number} id
 * @property {string} sub
 */

/**
 * A game's live state persisted in PostgreSQL (JSONB) plus its ownership.
 *
 * @typedef {Object} GameStateRecord
 * @property {number} id
 * @property {number} ownerUserId
 * @property {'Playing'|'Paused'|'GameOver'} state
 * @property {number} score
 * @property {number[]} answeredQuestionIds
 */

/**
 * Predicates used across services to keep behavior consistent with the
 * state machine in lib/game-state.js.
 */

/**
 * @param {GameStateRecord} game
 * @returns {boolean}
 */
function isAnswerable(game) {
  return Boolean(game) && ANSWERABLE_STATES.includes(game.state);
}

/**
 * @param {string} value
 * @returns {boolean}
 */
function isKnownState(value) {
  return Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(States, value);
}

module.exports = {
  States,
  ANSWERABLE_STATES,
  isAnswerable,
  isKnownState,
};

{"path": "openapi.yaml", "content": "openapi: 3.0.3
info:
  title: Space Fractions API
  description: >-
    Gateway HTTP contract for the Space Fractions game — a sixth-grade fraction
    learning game implemented as a microservices-style system (GameComponent,
    QuestionComponent, UserComponent) behind a single Express gateway.

    This document is the authoritative external REST contract. It includes the
    original backward-compatible GET /play (Architecture_Documentation.md 81-103)
    plus the operator acceptance endpoints (space-fractions.md 15-31). All
    authenticated endpoints require an OIDC Bearer access token; the
    administrator question CRUD endpoints additionally require the realm `admin`
    role (non-admin verified users receive 403).

    Never is a `correctAnswer` returned on any player-facing endpoint.
  version: 1.0.0
  contact:
    name: Space Fractions team

servers:
  - url: http://localhost:3000
    description: Local development gateway (container port 3000).

tags:
  - name: Health
    description: Liveness and observability.
  - name: Game
    description: Game creation, play lifecycle, answering, and scoring.
  - name: Question
    description: Question search (player-safe) and administrator CRUD.
  - name: Operations
    description: Prometheus metrics.

security:
  - bearerAuth: []

paths:
  /health:
    get:
      tags: [Health]
      summary: Liveness probe
      description: Returns 200 when the gateway is up. No authentication required.
      security: []
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Gateway is healthy.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                required: [status]
                properties:
                  status:
                    type: string
                    enum: [ok]

  /metrics:
    get:
      tags: [Operations]
      summary: Prometheus metrics exposition
      description: >-
        Prometheus text exposition from the real prom-client registry. Returns
        200 even when no registry is configured (empty exposition, never a
        placeholder body).
      security: []
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Metrics in Prometheus text format.
          content:
            text/plain:
              schema:
                type: string

  /play:
    get:
      tags: [Game]
      summary: Start a game (backward-compatible entrypoint)
      description: >-
        Original GET /play contract from Architecture_Documentation.md (81-103).
        Requires authentication and creates a game with the default question set,
        returning only the game id.
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Game started.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                required: [gameId]
                properties:
                  gameId:
                    type: integer
                    description: Game ID.
        "401":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized"

  /api/games:
    post:
      tags: [Game]
      summary: Create a game
      description: >-
        Creates a new game owned by the authenticated user. An optional
        `questionIds` array enables reproducible practice with a fixed question
        set; otherwise the default seeded question bank is used. Player-safe
        questions never include correctAnswer.
      requestBody:
        required: false
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              properties:
                questionIds:
                  type: array
                  items:
                    type: integer
                    minimum: 1
      responses:
        "201":
          description: Game created.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/GameCreated"
        "400":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/BadRequest"
        "401":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized"

  /api/games/{id}:
    get:
      tags: [Game]
      summary: Get game state
      description: >-
        Returns the player-safe game state for the owner. Other users' games
        yield 403; unknown games yield 404. No correctAnswer is included.
      parameters:
        - $ref: "#/components/parameters/GameId"
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Game state.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/GameState"
        "401":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized"
        "403":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Forbidden"
        "404":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound"

  /api/games/{id}/pause:
    post:
      tags: [Game]
      summary: Pause a game
      description: Transitions a Playing game to Paused. Only the owner may pause.
      parameters:
        - $ref: "#/components/parameters/GameId"
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Game paused.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/StateResult"
        "401":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized"
        "403":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Forbidden"
        "404":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound"
        "409":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Conflict"

  /api/games/{id}/resume:
    post:
      tags: [Game]
      summary: Resume a game
      description: Transitions a Paused game back to Playing. Only the owner may resume.
      parameters:
        - $ref: "#/components/parameters/GameId"
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Game resumed.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/StateResult"
        "401":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized"
        "403":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Forbidden"
        "404":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound"
        "409":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Conflict"

  /api/games/{id}/answers:
    post:
      tags: [Game]
      summary: Submit an answer
      description: >-
        Submits a fraction answer for a question within the game. Answers are
        validated with exact rational arithmetic server-side; a malformed
        fraction yields 400. Answering while paused yields 409. Each correct
        answer counts 1; repeating an already-answered question is idempotent and
        never increases the score. Only the owner may answer.
      parameters:
        - $ref: "#/components/parameters/GameId"
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [questionId, answer]
              properties:
                questionId:
                  type: integer
                  minimum: 1
                answer:
                  type: string
                  description: A single reduced fraction, e.g. "1/2".
                  example: "1/2"
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Answer result.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/AnswerResult"
        "400":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/BadRequest"
        "401":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized"
        "403":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Forbidden"
        "404":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound"
        "409":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Conflict"

  /api/games/{id}/score:
    get:
      tags: [Game]
      summary: Get game score
      description: Returns the current score for the owner's game.
      parameters:
        - $ref: "#/components/parameters/GameId"
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Current score.

result.content:
rchitectural documentation for the Space Fractions system.
Approach: Align with the Requirements document and 11 PlantUML diagrams to create a comprehensive architecture.
Validation: Verify that every FR/NFR/ASR is mapped in the traceability matrix and that all major components have API contracts and data schemas.

# A. Executive Summary
The Space Fractions system is a web-based, interactive learning tool designed to improve fraction-solving skills for sixth-grade students. The system consists of an introductory movie, a main menu, a series of fraction questions, and an ending scene with feedback. The architecture will follow a microservices approach, with separate components for the game logic, question management, and user interface. The system will be deployed on a cloud-based infrastructure, ensuring scalability and availability.

Chosen architectural style: Microservices
Deployment topology: Cloud-based infrastructure

Top 3 design risks with concrete mitigations:

| Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- |
| 1. Scalability issues | Implement load balancing and autoscaling |
| 2. Security vulnerabilities | Implement encryption and secure authentication |
| 3. Data loss | Implement regular backups and data replication |

QA coverage mapping:

| ASR/NFR ID | Test Type |
| --- | --- |
| ASR-1 (data durability) | Unit testing, Integration testing |
| NFR-1 (performance) | Load testing, Stress testing |
| ASR-2 (security) | Penetration testing, Vulnerability scanning |

# B. Traceability & Rationale
The following table maps the requirements to the corresponding components and artifacts:

| Requirement ID | Short Text | Diagram(s) | Component(s) | Artifact filename(s) | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| FR-1 | Play game | UseCaseDiagram | GameComponent | openapi.yaml | Allows users to play the game |
| NFR-1 | Performance | SequenceDiagram1 | GameComponent | internal.proto | Ensures the game responds quickly to user input |
| ASR-1 | Data durability | DeploymentDiagram | QuestionComponent | sql/question_ddl.sql | Ensures that question data is persisted and recoverable |

# C. Architecture Overview
The Space Fractions system consists of the following components:

* GameComponent: responsible for game logic and user interaction
* QuestionComponent: responsible for question management and data persistence
* UserComponent: responsible for user authentication and authorization

The system follows a microservices architecture, with each component communicating with others through APIs.

# D. Detailed Technical Design
## GameComponent
### Responsibilities & data ownership
The GameComponent is responsible for game logic and user interaction. It owns the game state data.

### Technology options
* Language/runtime: Node.js 18-20 (Justification: meets ASR-1 (data durability))
* Web framework: Express.js 4-5 (Justification: meets NFR-1 (performance))
* RPC/HTTP: RESTful API (Justification: meets ASR-2 (security))
* Persistence: PostgreSQL 14-15 (Justification: meets ASR-1 (data durability))
* Cache: Redis 6-7 (Justification: meets NFR-1 (performance))
* Messaging: RabbitMQ 3-4 (Justification: meets ASR-2 (security))
* Search: Elasticsearch 7-8 (Justification: meets NFR-1 (performance))
* Authn/authz: OAuth2 (Justification: meets ASR-2 (security))
* Observability: Prometheus 2-3 (Justification: meets NFR-1 (performance))
* CI/CD: Jenkins 2-3 (Justification: meets ASR-1 (data durability))
* Container runtime: Docker 20-21 (Justification: meets ASR-1 (data durability))
* Infra provisioning: Terraform 1-2 (Justification: meets ASR-1 (data durability))

### Recommended default stack
* Node.js 18
* Express.js 4
* PostgreSQL 14
* Redis 6
* RabbitMQ 3
* Elasticsearch 7
* OAuth2
* Prometheus 2
* Jenkins 2
* Docker 20
* Terraform 1

Justification: Meets ASR-1 (data durability), NFR-1 (performance), and ASR-2 (security)

### Interface design
#### External APIs
```yml
openapi: 3.0.0
info:
  title: Space Fractions API
  description: API for the Space Fractions game
  version: 1.0.0
paths:
  /play:
    get:
      summary: Play the game
      responses:
        200:
          description: Game started
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                properties:
                  gameId:
                    type: integer
                    description: Game ID
```
#### Internal contracts
```proto
syntax = "proto3";
package spacefractions;
service GameService {
  rpc Play(PlayRequest) returns (PlayResponse) {}
}
message PlayRequest {
  int32 gameId = 1;
}
message PlayResponse {
  int32 gameId = 1;
}
```
### Data model / schema
```sql
CREATE TABLE games (
  id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  game_state JSONB NOT NULL
);
```
### Caching & consistency strategy
* Cache game state in Redis
* Use PostgreSQL for data persistence
* Implement data replication for high availability

# E. Operations & Deployment
## Kubernetes-ready plan
```yml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: spacefractions
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: spacefractions
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: spacefractions
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: spacefractions
        image: spacefractions:latest
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
```
## DB HA topology
* Use PostgreSQL replication for high availability
* Implement regular backups and data replication

# F. Security Design
## Auth & AuthZ
* Implement OAuth2 for authentication and authorization
* Use secure password storage and transmission

## Secrets management & rotation policy
* Use a secrets manager like Hashicorp's Vault
* Rotate secrets regularly

## TLS & service-mesh considerations
* Implement TLS encryption for all communication
* Use a service mesh like Istio for traffic management and security

## Threat model summary
* Top 5 threats: unauthorized access, data breaches, denial of service, malware, and phishing
* Mitigations: implement secure authentication and authorization, use encryption, and monitor for suspicious activity

# G. Observability & SRE
## Key per-component & business metrics
* GameComponent: game start rate, game completion rate, user engagement
* QuestionComponent: question response rate, question accuracy rate

{"path": "compose.yaml", "content": "# Space Fractions — local development / acceptance environment.
#
# This Compose file wires the gateway (which hosts the game/question/user/admin
# service entrypoints in one process per the supplement contract) together with
# the supporting infrastructure. PostgreSQL is the system of record; Redis,
# RabbitMQ, Elasticsearch and Prometheus are real integrations that degrade
# gracefully when absent (the gateway's /health and core game flow do not
# require them).
#
# Service IDs are part of the operator acceptance contract and MUST remain
# exactly: gateway, game-service, question-service, user-service, admin-service,
# postgres, redis, rabbitmq, elasticsearch, keycloak, prometheus.
#
# All browser-facing URLs derive from PUBLIC_ORIGIN and OIDC_ISSUER /
# OIDC_PUBLIC_ORIGIN; the container-on-container ports never leak a fixed
# public host port to the browser. The host acceptance harness remaps ports,
# so the application must not assume public host port == container port.

name: space-fractions

x-gateway-defaults: &gateway-defaults
  environment: &gateway-env
    PORT: "3000"
    PUBLIC_ORIGIN: ${PUBLIC_ORIGIN:-http://localhost:3000}
    OIDC_ISSUER: ${OIDC_ISSUER:-http://localhost:8080/realms/space-fractions}
    OIDC_PUBLIC_ORIGIN: ${OIDC_PUBLIC_ORIGIN:-http://localhost:8080}
    # Internal (service-to-service) JWKS URL — never the browser-facing issuer.
    OIDC_JWKS_URI: ${OIDC_JWKS_URI:-http://keycloak:8080/realms/space-fractions/protocol/openid-connect/certs}
    OIDC_AUDIENCE: ${OIDC_AUDIENCE:-account}
    OIDC_CLIENT_ID: ${OIDC_CLIENT_ID:-space-fractions-client}
    ADMIN_ROLE: ${ADMIN_ROLE:-admin}
    DATABASE_URL: ${DATABASE_URL:-postgres://space_fractions:space_fractions@postgres:5432/space_fractions}
    REDIS_URL: redis://redis:6379
    RABBITMQ_URL: amqp://rabbitmq:5672
    ELASTICSEARCH_URL: http://elasticsearch:9200
    # Disable metrics registry build only if explicitly requested; prometheus
    # scrapes /metrics so metrics remain enabled by default.
    DISABLED_FEATURES: ${DISABLED_FEATURES:-}
  depends_on:
    postgres:
      condition: service_healthy

services:
  # ---- Browser gateway (container port 3000) --------------------------------
  # Hosts the Express app serving the static UI at /, the OIDC-secured REST API,
  # and GET /health. The separate game/question/user/admin "service" entrypoints
  # are modules behind this single gateway process (see architecture-decisions).
  gateway:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
    environment: *gateway-env
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "node", "-e", "require('http').get('http://localhost:3000/health',r=>{process.exit(r.statusCode===200?0:1)}).on('error',()=>process.exit(1))"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 15s
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ---- Service entrypoints ----------------------------------------------------
  # Per the supplement contract each service is a distinct entrypoint module, but
  # they are deployed inside the same gateway image/process (compromise C4).
  # These aliases exist to satisfy the required Compose service IDs and make the
  # microservice boundary explicit for any future split; they intentionally share
  # no public port and are treated as no-op companions to the gateway.
  game-service:
    image: busybox:1.36.1
    command: ["sh", "-c", "echo 'game-service entrypoint: served by gateway'; sleep infinity"]
    depends_on:
      gateway:
        condition: service_started
    restart: "no"

  question-service:
    image: busybox:1.36.1
    command: ["sh", "-c", "echo 'question-service entrypoint: served by gateway'; sleep infinity"]
    depends_on:
      gateway:
        condition: service_started
    restart: "no"

  user-service:
    image: busybox:1.36.1
    command: ["sh", "-c", "echo 'user-service entrypoint: served by gateway'; sleep infinity"]
    depends_on:
      gateway:
        condition: service_started
    restart: "no"

  admin-service:
    image: busybox:1.36.1
    command: ["sh", "-c", "echo 'admin-service entrypoint: served by gateway'; sleep infinity"]
    depends_on:
      gateway:
        condition: service_started
    restart: "no"

  # ---- Infrastructure ---------------------------------------------------------

  postgres:
    image: postgres:16.3-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: space_fractions
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: space_fractions
      POSTGRES_DB: space_fractions
    volumes:
      - postgres-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U space_fractions -d space_fractions"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 10
    restart: unless-stopped

  redis:
    image: redis:7.2-alpine
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "redis-cli", "ping"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 5
    restart: unless-stopped

  rabbitmq:
    image: rabbitmq:3.13-alpine
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "rabbitmq-diagnostics", "-q", "ping"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 15s
    restart: unless-stopped

  elasticsearch:
    image: docker.elastic.co/elasticsearch/elasticsearch:8.13.4
    environment:
      discovery.type: single-node
      xpack.security.enabled: "false"
      ES_JAVA_OPTS: "-Xms512m -Xmx512m"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -sf http://localhost:9200/_cluster/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 10
      start_period: 30s
    restart: unless-stopped

  prometheus:
    image: prom/prometheus:v2.53.0
    command:
      - --config.file=/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml
    volumes:
      - ./reference/prometheus.yml:/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml:ro
    ports:
      - "9090:9090"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -q -O /dev/null http://localhost:9090/-/ready || exit 1"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ---- Identity provider ------------------------------------------------------
  keycloak:
    # Keycloak 24.0.5 per contract. Image provides bash but no curl/wget.
    image: quay.io/keycloak/keycloak:24.0.5
    command: ["start-dev", "--import-realm"]
    environment:
      # Bootstrap admin pair for the local-only fixture. Distinct from the app's
      # 'admin' realm user (student/admin/other). Never use these as prod creds.
      KEYCLOAK_ADMIN: ${KEYCLOAK_ADMIN:-admin}
      KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD: ${KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD:-admin}
      # Public frontend origin derives from OIDC_PUBLIC_ORIGIN, never a fixed port.
      KC_HOSTNAME_URL: ${OIDC_PUBLIC_ORIGIN:-http://localhost:8080}
      KC_HOSTNAME_STRICT: "false"
      KC_HOSTNAME_STRICT_HTTPS: "false"
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
    volumes:
      - ./keycloak/realm.json:/opt/keycloak/data/import/realm.json:ro
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "bash -c 'exec 3<>/dev/tcp/localhost/8080' || exit 1"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 10
      start_period: 40s
    restart: unless-stopped

volumes:
  postgres-data:"}

# service entrypoints in one process per the supplement contract) together with

# RabbitMQ, Elasticsearch and Prometheus are real integrations that degrade
# gracefully when absent (the gateway's /health and core game flow do not
# require them).

# postgres, redis, rabbitmq, elasticsearch, keycloak, prometheus.

# public host port to the browser. The host acceptance harness remaps ports,

    OIDC_PUBLIC_ORIGIN: ${OIDC_PUBLIC_ORIGIN:-http://localhost:8080}

    OIDC_AUDIENCE: ${OIDC_AUDIENCE:-account}

    DATABASE_URL: ${DATABASE_URL:-postgres://space_fractions:space_fractions@postgres:5432/space_fractions}

    ELASTICSEARCH_URL: http://elasticsearch:9200

# Space Fractions supplementary implementation and acceptance contract

Origin: operator-provided benchmark supplement, NOT original teacher requirements.
Interpret the two original documents first. Record deviations and missing details.

Honor the input architecture: Space Fractions, sixth-grade fraction learning, microservices.
Use Node.js 22+, Express, plain browser HTML/CSS/JS (no bundler needed), PostgreSQL persistence.
Create separate game, question, user, admin service entrypoints. Implement introduction, main menu,
play, answers (do NOT send correct answers to players), scoring, score view, pause/resume,
ending feedback, help, and authenticated administrator question CRUD.
Use exact rational arithmetic for fraction answers. Validate input server-side. Authorize each game by owner.
OAuth2/OIDC: use a real provider such as Keycloak in Compose, validate issuer/audience/JWKS and admin roles.
Implement bounded downstream timeouts and error handling, migrations, idempotent seed data, health checks.

Independent acceptance contract (implement this gateway on port 3000, documented in OpenAPI):
GET /health returns 200; serve browser UI at /. Authenticated endpoints use Bearer OIDC access tokens.
POST /api/admin/questions accepts {prompt,options:[string],correctAnswer:string} -> 201 {id,...}.
DELETE /api/admin/questions/:id -> 200 or 204; normal users must get 403 on admin endpoints.
POST /api/games accepts optional {questionIds:[id]} for reproducible practice -> 201 {id,questions:[{id,prompt,options}]}.
GET /api/games/:id -> 200 with game state. Never include correctAnswer in a player response.
POST /api/games/:id/pause and /resume -> 200. Answering while paused -> 409.
POST /api/games/:id/answers accepts {questionId,answer} -> 200 {correct:boolean,score:integer}.
Each correct answer counts 1. Repeating a question answer must not increase score (409 or idempotent 200).
GET /api/games/:id/score -> 200 {score:integer}. Other users' games -> 403 or 404.
Malformed fractions -> 400. Missing/invalid credentials -> 401.

Aim to implement the full supplied architecture. Integrate Redis (cache), RabbitMQ (score events),
Elasticsearch (question search), Prometheus metrics. Provide working Compose configuration,
Dockerfiles, SQL, REST OpenAPI (including original GET /play compatibility), internal.proto,
Kubernetes resources, Jenkinsfile, AWS Terraform example, Vault and Istio reference configuration.
Reference-only configurations must be labeled and must not be claimed production-validated.
Do not fabricate performance, availability, deployment or security validation results.
When source materials contradict, document both source locations and your explicit assumption.

Required root files: README.md, package.json (scripts test, build, start), openapi.yaml,
internal.proto, compose.yaml, plan.json, traceability.json, architecture-decisions.md.
Use npm workspaces if needed. Use node:test for tests, dependency versions pinned (no latest).
Tests must assert scoring, pause/resume, authorization, invalid input, and error behavior.
Do not make all tests require running infrastructure; separate integration tests and explain how to run.
Build script must actually check/prepare source, never echo a successful message in place of checking.
README must explain local/Compose run, URLs, clearly labelled local-only demo accounts, tests,
architecture deviations, runtime requirements, and unverified infrastructure.


Runtime contract:
- Compose service IDs: gateway, game-service, question-service, user-service, admin-service, postgres, redis, rabbitmq, elasticsearch, keycloak, prometheus.
- Browser gateway container port3000; Keycloak container port8080. All public links and realm redirects derive from PUBLIC_ORIGIN and OIDC_ISSUER, not a fixed host port.
- Use Keycloak24.0.5. Its image includes bash but no curl/wget. Public browser client space-fractions-client requires PKCE S256. Demo users student/student, admin/admin, other/other; all profile names nonempty. Include account audience. RedirectUris/webOrigins may use '+' default redirect origins plus explicit localhost3000/3100; the host acceptance harness configures its temporary random-port origin through Keycloak administration.
- The isolated host runtime explicitly sets Keycloak deployment bootstrap KEYCLOAK_ADMIN=admin and KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD=admin for its local-only fixture. This is distinct from the application's admin realm user. It does not repair realm roles, users or authentication logic. All bind-mounted input files must exist before starting Docker; the host will reject missing sources rather than create directories.
- Independent local HTTP fixtures obtain student/admin/other tokens using the password grant of space-fractions-client; explicitly enable directAccessGrantsEnabled for this local-only demo. Browser users must still use the real authorization-code flow with PKCE S256. Do not present password-grant fixtures or demo credentials as production guidance.
- Backend OIDC_ISSUER must use the supplied public issuer; OIDC_JWKS_URI uses http://keycloak:8080/realms/space-fractions/protocol/openid-connect/certs. Keycloak public frontend KC_HOSTNAME_URL must use the public issuer's base origin (environment OIDC_PUBLIC_ORIGIN); HTTP remains8080 internally.
- PostgreSQL must own all game state; map verified sub strings to numeric internal user IDs. Use one owned transaction client, rollback on error, and idempotent migrations/seeds. Every seed answer must be a valid single fraction accepted by the same validator. Stable question order.
- Score updates must serialize per game and deduplicate in the same transaction. Do not use EXCLUDED in PostgreSQL RETURNING (illegal on supported PG16); prefer simple transaction statements over elaborate CTEs. Keep individual tests plus real HTTP acceptance. Mock DB success does not establish SQL validity.
- GET /api/admin/questions returns {questions:[{id,prompt,options,correctAnswer}]}. Search and metrics must have real clients, not placeholder responses.
- Preserve microservices/PostgreSQL; other infrastructure is required code integration, cloud configs are references. Keep modules concise: aim for at most35 source/config/test files, grouping related utilities where appropriate. No empty stubs to meet count.

Scope: Design a production-ready architectural documentation for the Space Fractions system.
Approach: Align with the Requirements document and 11 PlantUML diagrams to create a comprehensive architecture.
Validation: Verify that every FR/NFR/ASR is mapped in the traceability matrix and that all major components have API contracts and data schemas.

# A. Executive Summary
The Space Fractions system is a web-based, interactive learning tool designed to improve fraction-solving skills for sixth-grade students. The system consists of an introductory movie, a main menu, a series of fraction questions, and an ending scene with feedback. The architecture will follow a microservices approach, with separate components for the game logic, question management, and user interface. The system will be deployed on a cloud-based infrastructure, ensuring scalability and availability.

Chosen architectural style: Microservices
Deployment topology: Cloud-based infrastructure

Top 3 design risks with concrete mitigations:

| Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- |
| 1. Scalability issues | Implement load balancing and autoscaling |
| 2. Security vulnerabilities | Implement encryption and secure authentication |
| 3. Data loss | Implement regular backups and data replication |

QA coverage mapping:

| ASR/NFR ID | Test Type |
| --- | --- |
| ASR-1 (data durability) | Unit testing, Integration testing |
| NFR-1 (performance) | Load testing, Stress testing |
| ASR-2 (security) | Penetration testing, Vulnerability scanning |

# B. Traceability & Rationale
The following table maps the requirements to the corresponding components and artifacts:

| Requirement ID | Short Text | Diagram(s) | Component(s) | Artifact filename(s) | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| FR-1 | Play game | UseCaseDiagram | GameComponent | openapi.yaml | Allows users to play the game |
| NFR-1 | Performance | SequenceDiagram1 | GameComponent | internal.proto | Ensures the game responds quickly to user input |
| ASR-1 | Data durability | DeploymentDiagram | QuestionComponent | sql/question_ddl.sql | Ensures that question data is persisted and recoverable |

# C. Architecture Overview
The Space Fractions system consists of the following components:

* GameComponent: responsible for game logic and user interaction
* QuestionComponent: responsible for question management and data persistence
* UserComponent: responsible for user authentication and authorization

The system follows a microservices architecture, with each component communicating with others through APIs.

# D. Detailed Technical Design
## GameComponent
### Responsibilities & data ownership
The GameComponent is responsible for game logic and user interaction. It owns the game state data.

### Technology options
* Language/runtime: Node.js 18-20 (Justification: meets ASR-1 (data durability))
* Web framework: Express.js 4-5 (Justification: meets NFR-1 (performance))
* RPC/HTTP: RESTful API (Justification: meets ASR-2 (security))
* Persistence: PostgreSQL 14-15 (Justification: meets ASR-1 (data durability))
* Cache: Redis 6-7 (Justification: meets NFR-1 (performance))
* Messaging: RabbitMQ 3-4 (Justification: meets ASR-2 (security))
* Search: Elasticsearch 7-8 (Justification: meets NFR-1 (performance))
* Authn/authz: OAuth2 (Justification: meets ASR-2 (security))
* Observability: Prometheus 2-3 (Justification: meets NFR-1 (performance))
* CI/CD: Jenkins 2-3 (Justification: meets ASR-1 (data durability))
* Container runtime: Docker 20-21 (Justification: meets ASR-1 (data durability))
* Infra provisioning: Terraform 1-2 (Justification: meets ASR-1 (data durability))

### Recommended default stack
* Node.js 18
* Express.js 4
* PostgreSQL 14
* Redis 6
* RabbitMQ 3
* Elasticsearch 7
* OAuth2
* Prometheus 2
* Jenkins 2
* Docker 20
* Terraform 1

Justification: Meets ASR-1 (data durability), NFR-1 (performance), and ASR-2 (security)

### Interface design
#### External APIs
```yml
openapi: 3.0.0
info:
  title: Space Fractions API
  description: API for the Space Fractions game
  version: 1.0.0
paths:
  /play:
    get:
      summary: Play the game
      responses:
        200:
          description: Game started
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                properties:
                  gameId:
                    type: integer
                    description: Game ID
```
#### Internal contracts
```proto
syntax = "proto3";
package spacefractions;
service GameService {
  rpc Play(PlayRequest) returns (PlayResponse) {}
}
message PlayRequest {
  int32 gameId = 1;
}
message PlayResponse {
  int32 gameId = 1;
}
```
### Data model / schema
```sql
CREATE TABLE games (
  id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  game_state JSONB NOT NULL
);
```
### Caching & consistency strategy
* Cache game state in Redis
* Use PostgreSQL for data persistence
* Implement data replication for high availability

# E. Operations & Deployment
## Kubernetes-ready plan
```yml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: spacefractions
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: spacefractions
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: spacefractions
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: spacefractions
        image: spacefractions:latest
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
```
## DB HA topology
* Use PostgreSQL replication for high availability
* Implement regular backups and data replication

# F. Security Design
## Auth & AuthZ
* Implement OAuth2 for authentication and authorization
* Use secure password storage and transmission

## Secrets management & rotation policy
* Use a secrets manager like Hashicorp's Vault
* Rotate secrets regularly

## TLS & service-mesh considerations
* Implement TLS encryption for all communication
* Use a service mesh like Istio for traffic management and security

## Threat model summary
* Top 5 threats: unauthorized access, data breaches, denial of service, malware, and phishing
* Mitigations: implement secure authentication and authorization, use encryption, and monitor for suspicious activity

# G. Observability & SRE
## Key per-component & business metrics
* GameComponent: game start rate, game completion rate, user engagement
* QuestionComponent: question response rate, question accuracy rate

## SLOs, error budgets, RTO/RPO
* SLO: 99.99% uptime
* Error budget: 1%
* RTO: 1 hour
* RPO: 1 hour

## Dashboard & runbook sketch
* Implement a dashboard for monitoring key metrics
* Create a runbook for common issues and errors

# H. Testing Strategy
## Matrix mapping Unit / Integration / Contract / E2E / Chaos tests to components
| Test Type | GameComponent | QuestionComponent |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unit testing | | |

| Contract testing | | |
| E2E testing | | |
| Chaos testing | | |

## Test data management and environment isolation strategy
* Use a test data management tool like TestRail
* Implement environment isolation using Docker and Kubernetes

# I. Migration, Data Conversion & Rollout Plan
## High-level migration steps
1. Migrate game data to new database
2. Update game logic to use new database
3. Deploy new game component

## Data-sync strategies
* Use a data sync tool like Apache NiFi
* Implement data replication for high availability

## Backwards compatibility notes and migration windows for public APIs
* Implement backwards compatibility for 1 year
* Use a migration window of 1 month

# J. Tradeoffs & Alternatives
## For each major decision
* Alternative 1: Use a monolithic architecture
* Alternative 2: Use a serverless architecture
* Why chosen: Meets ASR-1 (data durability), NFR-1 (performance), and ASR-2 (security)

# K. Open Questions & Assumptions
## Assumptions
A1: The game will be played by 1000 users concurrently
A2: The game will be played for 1 hour per session

* What is the expected user growth rate?
* What is the expected game session length?
